item.title: TEDlm — domain-centric protein language model beats ESM-2-3B on CATH S40 remote homology at 650M params (AUROC1 0.28 vs 0.22); TEDlm3D with distance-guided contact loss reaches 0.50, matching Foldseek from sequence alone (Jones lab, UCL, bioRxiv); de novo conformation-selective miniprotein modulators of focal adhesion kinase — 33/96 designs modulate activity, low-nM inhibitors and 2×+ activators, cross-kinase redesign to Src (Baker lab, bioRxiv); AlphaFold3 audit across 5 application areas — uneven performance, training-set-adjacency dependence, model confidence fails on protein-RNA (Beltrao lab, U Fribourg/Lausanne, bioRxiv); ESM3-SM guided decoding + Topoly Alexander-polynomial scoring hits 89% knotted-protein success vs 0.5% unguided diffusion, 84% sequence perturbation before knot breaks (bioRxiv); asymmetric structural transfer — language-to-biology transfer strengthens with scale (drop 0.08), biology-to-language decays toward chance (drop 0.36), replicated across ESM-2 and ProtBERT (bioRxiv)
item.description: Monday morning briefing — five items, all posted 2026-07-13 or 2026-07-14, strong methodological day. First, Wei/Kandathil/Buchan/Jones (UCL, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.09.737428, posted 2026-07-13): TEDlm — masked language model pre-trained on structurally-defined domain segments from The Encyclopedia of Domains rather than full-length UniRef sequences. Standard MLM objective; TEDlm3D variant adds a distance-guided contact loss supervising attention maps against Cα–Cα geometry during pre-training. On CATH S40 remote-homology (<40% identity), 650M TEDlm scores AUROC1 0.28 at final layer vs ESM-2 3B at 0.22 — domain-centric pretraining beats 5× parameter scale-up. TEDlm3D reaches 0.50, approaching Foldseek's structure-based 0.53 from sequence at inference. Contact signal is in the encoder itself: attention-map probes and categorical Jacobian recover contact structure, not just a trained head. Zero-shot Molecular Function prediction substantially better than ESM-2; biophysical property tasks (dominated by local composition) comparable. Direct implication for antibody-LM builders: antibody variable domains are exactly one TED domain, argues restricted-domain pretraining (AntiBERTy, AbLang, IgLM) was correct choice; TEDlm3D contact loss transfers cleanly to paired-structure pretraining with SAbDab/AF3-multimer/IgFold coordinates. Second, Bauer/Lee et al./Baker (UW IPD + collaborators, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.10.737808, posted 2026-07-13, body not yet rendered — abstract-only): de novo genetically encoded miniprotein binders targeting focal adhesion kinase (FAK) with conformation-selective framing — each design targeted to stabilize a specific FAK conformational state (active vs inactive). 96 designs → 33 modulate kinase activity (~34% hit rate consistent with modern RFdiffusion+ProteinMPNN+AF filter pipelines). Top 4 characterized: 2 inhibitors with low-nM IC50s, 2 activators (>2× activity potentiation). Modulators preserve in-vitro directional effects in cells. Cross-kinase transfer: FAK inhibitors redesigned computationally to target Src kinase work — platform-level result. Design pipeline not spelled out in abstract but authorship + framing implies standard RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN + AF-filter stack; novelty is conformation-selective scaffolding and demonstration that both inhibition and activation are accessible from the same platform. Complements antibody engineering — intracellular targets are outside the antibody-accessible space. Third, Follonier/Liu et al./Beltrao (U Fribourg + U Lausanne, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.13.738147, posted 2026-07-13, body not yet rendered — abstract-only): audit of AlphaFold3 across five application areas — ubiquitinated protein structure, TCR–peptide-MHC recognition, antibody-antigen complexes, protein-RNA, protein-lipid. Headline: AF3's extension to new biomolecule types shows less consistent performance and generalisation than AF2's monomer/multimer gains. Accuracy in several tasks depends on presence of related complexes in the training set (memorization/adjacency effect). Specific critical finding: in protein-RNA predictions, model confidence fails to separate genuine from decoy interaction partners — confidence metric untrustworthy for RNA-target screening. Antibody-antigen task included; specific number pending body render but consistent with "good in favourable settings, dependent on training-set overlap, less broadly generalisable than AF2" — matches anecdotal experience with novel epitopes and unusual CDR H3 / germline usage. Practical frame: AF3 is powerful for hypothesis generation and prioritisation but confidence metrics must be used with awareness of training-set overlap on an application-by-application basis. Fourth, "Advancing Knotted Protein Design with ESM3" (bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.05.07.723606, posted 2026-07-14): ESM3-SM (1.4B params, smallest open-source variant, fp16 on NVIDIA A10G via Modal) with derivative-free guided decoding using Topoly Alexander-polynomial scoring (30 random-projection stochastic closures per evaluation) to design knotted proteins. Guided ESM3 achieves 89% success (95% CI 81–94%) vs ~0.5% for unguided diffusion (RFdiffusion, EvoDiff) — dramatic gap but explicitly guided-vs-unguided not architecture-matched. Robustness: 84% of sequence must be perturbed on average before knot breaks; loss follows sharp threshold not gradual degradation; structural drift (RMSD) accumulates well before topology fails — topology more robust than specific 3D arrangement in ESM3 representation. Generated knot types include trefoil (33), figure-eight (10), torus 5₂ (10), plus 8₁₉, 9₄₄, 9₄₅. No close sequence similarity to known knotted proteins (KnotProt/AlphaKnot 2.0) — not memorization. Practical for structurally unusual antibody scaffolds — cyclic-permuted VHHs, disulphide-constrained topologies. Fifth, "Asymmetric Structural Transfer Between Natural Language and Biological Foundation Models" (bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.09.737502, posted 2026-07-13, abstract only): reverse-transfer study asking whether protein LMs fine-tuned on English structural tasks acquire zero-shot linguistic competence, in the same way English-fine-tuned LMs had been shown to acquire zero-shot protein-homology discrimination. Answer: reverse transfer is consistently weak, does not exceed matched-token controls, does not scale, does not generalize. Architecture-matched 2×2 with known training data (eliminates pretraining-contamination confound): language→biology off-domain drop 0.08 vs biology→language 0.36. Scaling widens the gap — language-to-biology strengthens with size, biology-to-language decays toward chance. Replicated across ESM-2 and ProtBERT families. Implication: initializing specialized biological models from general-purpose LMs is asymmetrically favoured over the reverse; "biological sequences are just another language" fails in operationally symmetric sense.

item.title: Night: BCR-Mistral — 500M-parameter decoder-only DNA BCR language model beats ESM-2-650M and Ab-RoBERTa on MS-associated repertoire embedding across 11.5M IGH sequences (Krishnan/Macklin, U Colorado Anschutz, bioRxiv); RFdiffusion+ProteinMPNN motif-scaffolding of N-Myc TAD yields single-digit-nM Aurora-A miniprotein inhibitors with crystal-structure-verified αG-helix + activation-loop convergent signature (Bayliss lab, Leeds, bioRxiv); Blood Transcriptional Module aggregation beats gene-level features by 14–25 AUC points on pan-vaccine (influenza/HepB/YF) high-responder prediction across 1,032 participants (Tomic/Przytycki, Boston U, bioRxiv)
item.description: Monday night supplement — three items, all posted 2026-07-13. First, Peet/Krishnan/Macklin (University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.07.735316): BCR-Mistral — nucleotide-level decoder-only DNA foundation model for BCR IGH sequences, downscaled from Mistral-7B architecture; three variants at 100M/300M/500M parameters, 500M model kept. Trained on ~2M heterogeneous OPIG OAS IGH sequences selected by iterative random sampling in 7-mer Euclidean space; nucleotide-level tokenization, random rotation, up to two 20-nt attention masks, up to one-third length truncation as augmentation; AdamW, effective batch 2400, 8 AMD MI100 GPUs. Outperforms ESM-2-650M and Ab-RoBERTa on same-disease-different-patient embedding triplet distances and cosine similarity; protein-tokenized variant of same architecture on same corpus performs worse than DNA variant, arguing nucleotide tokens capture codon-bias / silent-mutation signal beyond protein level. Downstream: 3-layer MLP classifier (256/128/64) on last-token embeddings for 5-way disease classification (healthy / autoimmune / infectious / other / MS); custom "dynamic exclusion" loss progressively drops MS sequences confidently classified as non-MS from the loss (analogous to semi-hard example mining), raising held-out precision. Study-grouped (not patient-grouped) CV folds surface study-driven artifacts. Data foundation: exhaustive NCBI SRA reanalysis of "multiple sclerosis" runs (December 2024 snapshot) with manual metadata curation + TRUST4 assembly + OPIG OAS = 11.5M IGH sequences from ~800 patients, 2.8M with full VDJ. Patient-level: 128-waypoint fixed-D repertoire embedding via joint reconstruction+contrastive optimization in hidden-state space; XGBoost on waypoint + sequence-classification inputs; ROC AUC >0.8 for MS vs healthy/infectious, lower for MS vs other autoimmune. Validation: correctly ranks 3/4 known PLP1c-binding myelin-specific IgGs above isotype control; longitudinal fingolimod/natalizumab treatment reduces disease-associated repertoire fraction (n small, not individually significant but direction consistent). Confirmed antibody binding to O4+ oligodendrocytes by flow. Code (upon publication) at github.com/krishnanlab/bcr-mistral-final; weights + processed data at Zenodo 20432913. Second, Miles/Bayliss (University of Leeds + University of Oxford Gergely lab, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.12.737516): RFdiffusion motif-scaffolding of N-Myc TAD residues 73–84 (short) and 73–89 (long) with Aurora-A hotspots, ~3,893 backbones across two motif sets, ProteinMPNN 1–2 seqs/backbone, AF2-initial-guess filter (iPAE<10, pLDDT>84, 2.5–3% hit rate); 17 designs selected. 15 express in E. coli, 8 inhibit Aurora-A ADP-Glo with fittable IC50s. Top designs DBS1 (IC50 12 nM, KD 0.9 nM by ITC — sub-nanomolar), DBS5 (IC50 16 nM), DBL5 (IC50 31 nM, KD 3 nM). ~1000× affinity gain over parent N-Myc peptide (KD ~12 μM). 9 crystal structures at 1.79–2.9 Å reveal convergent design signature — extensive αG-helix engagement via C-terminal helix + hydrogen bond / main-chain contact to activation loop; weak binders have shorter/bent C-terminal helices. DBL5 H55A mutation removes activation-loop H-bond → 10× IC50 loss to 425 nM, causally confirms the pattern. Aurora-B selectivity: DBS1 retains weak Aurora-B activity (100× less than Aurora-A), other selective binders essentially inactive on Aurora-B in ADP-Glo. Kinase-structure basis for selectivity: M233→L289 in P+1 pocket + non-conserved αG-helix residues Y334/Q335 in Aurora-A vs Aurora-B/C. Cellular: HeLa GFP-fusion transfections reduce Aurora-A T288 autophosphorylation at spindle poles for DBL5 and DBS1; DBS1 (only) also modestly reduces Histone H3 pS10; IP-MS: DBL5/DBS2/DBS5 pull down only Aurora-A + TPX2 as common interactors (24–42 proteins each), DBS1 promiscuous (215 interactors including MARK2, MELK). AF3 ternary Aurora-A/DBS1/TPX2 model supports simultaneous binding (ipTM 0.81/0.96). Design-to-hit ratio unusually good (17 designs, 13 with measurable inhibition, sub-nM hit) argues motif-scaffolding from natural weak binder is lower-variance than de novo. Third, Hao/Tomic/Przytycki (Boston University Bioinformatics + NEIDL + Chobanian & Avedisian SOM, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.08.737303): interpretable ML for shared and vaccine-specific immune architectures. Harmonized ISDR/HIPC dataset, 1,032 participants with matched pre/post-vax transcriptomics + ~day-28 antibody titers across influenza (n=776), HepB (n=160), and yellow fever (n=96). Independent random-forest classifiers per pathogen. Blood Transcriptional Module aggregation dominates raw gene-level features: AUC lifts 0.56→0.78 (HepB), 0.54→0.70 (influenza), 0.56→0.81 (YF). Permutation feature-importance: HepB driven by Th2 differentiation, integrin leukocyte migration, pDCs, M1 macrophages, B-cell modules; influenza by CD4+ T, M2 macrophage, c-MYC + mitotic cell cycle; yellow fever by BCR signaling, B-cell development, CORO1A-DEF6, MAIT, NK. Surrogate decision trees extract if-then rules with numerical thresholds. Cross-pathogen concordance identifies 4 shared transcriptional modules. Age but not sex residualization applied. Predicts peak (day-28) titer despite paper's framing; four shared modules are consistently-predictive-across-independent-models rather than jointly-modeled. Operational take for antibody engineers: BTM signatures identified are candidate stratification biomarkers for enriching high-responder repertoires in downstream discovery.

item.title: Afternoon: CADAbRe — structure- and energy-based synthetic antibody repertoire design v2 (Fleishman lab, Weizmann, bioRxiv) — 5×10^8 designed Fabs, 12/13 phage hits match designed sequence, EC50 0.3–11 nM against four unrelated antigens, developability on par with clinical antibodies; mini-19 — de novo CD81-LEL binder for HCV entry blockade via RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN + AlphaFold2 with multi-model backbone-convergence filter (Cho/Kim, Yonsei + Institut Pasteur Korea, bioRxiv) — 0.5 nM KD, HCV IC50 1.2 nM, thermostable to 95°C; HB148-M4 — four SHMs (G26E/T28I/S53P/Y58F) rescue IGHV3-53 germline antibody breadth to Omicron BA.1/BA.4-5, transferable to 3 of 4 other IGHV3-53 antibodies (Cao lab, Adv Sci)
item.description: Afternoon supplement — three antibody/protein-design items today. First, Tennenhouse/Fleishman (Weizmann Institute of Science, bioRxiv 10.64898/2025.12.10.693474 v2, posted 2026-07-13): CADAbRe — end-to-end computational design of an entire synthetic antibody repertoire with drug-like properties. Pipeline: (1) combine all human V+J germline segments, graft 141 experimentally-determined CDR H3s, generate ~150k combinations; (2) atomistic modeling with CUMAb + independent A-Body-Builder-2 fold check, flag disagreements as prone to misfolding; (3) EpiNNet ML strategy selects freely-combinable germline+H3 sets from Rosetta energy + foldability labels — 10 sets containing 35k sequences, 85% predicted stable, >700 unique light-heavy V-gene pairs (2 orders of magnitude more than recent synthetic repertoires); (4) Rosetta atomistic H3 diversification with immutable stability-critical residues, developability filters (no Met/Cys/N-glycosylation). Largest set expanded to ~450 V-gene pairs, 240k designed H3s, assembled by one-pot Golden Gate + phage display of Fabs at <$10^-4 per variant, 10-day turnaround, 5×10^8 unique antibodies. Panning against HEWL, SARS-CoV-2 RBD, mouse FLT3, and Lujo virus spike: 13 designed binders from <150 sequenced colonies, 12/13 exactly match a designed sequence, spanning 5 heavy V genes, 6 light V genes, 6 parental H3 scaffolds; EC50 0.3–11 nM comparable to clinical benchmarks where available; 9 expressed cleanly as IgG1 with yields above historical average. Developability suite (nanoDSF, BVP/CIC, SEC/AC-SINS/DLS, HIC) benchmarked against 12 clinical-stage antibodies including Adalimumab and Pembrolizumab: all designs Tagg>74°C and Tm>69°C, most low nonspecific binding and low self-association; 3/9 flagged for hydrophobicity (2 of these against RBD, consistent with anti-RBD antibody class). Repertoire available for academic research. Second, An/Cho/Kim (Yonsei + Institut Pasteur Korea + POSTECH, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.10.737702, posted 2026-07-13): de novo mini-protein binder mini-19 targeting CD81 large extracellular loop to block HCV entry. RFdiffusion (60–80 aa, 3-helix bundle topology, hotspot at L162/V169/I182/F186, noise 0.5) → 5000 backbones → 44 pass pAE<5.99; ProteinMPNN 1000 sequences per scaffold → filter pAE<4.7; AlphaFold2 validation with critical methodological finding — truncated soluble CD81 template exposes hydrophobic surfaces naturally shielded by transmembrane region, driving off-target binding artifacts; single ipTM threshold insufficient, requires multi-model consensus (≥2 of 5 AF2 models agree on backbone conformation with ipTM>0.83 + pLDDT>85) to eliminate false positives. 20 leads → 15 express cleanly at tens of mg/L E. coli → 8 bind CD81-LEL by SPR at 1 μM. Lead mini-19: KD 0.5 nM (ka 7.4×10^5 M^-1 s^-1, kd 3.8×10^-4 s^-1), monodisperse monomer, α-helical CD signature retained to 95°C without cooperative unfolding, HCVcc IC50 1.2 nM, native cell-surface CD81 recognition confirmed by flow cytometry and super-resolution imaging; sibling mini-20 same scaffold 48× weaker at 24 nM. MD suggests structural clamp locking closed conformation. Transferable ipTM+backbone-convergence recipe for any design task on truncated soluble receptor construct. Third, Cao lab et al. (Adv Sci, DOI 10.1002/advs.76522; preprint bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.03.20.713312, published 2026-07-13): breadth-restoration by database-mined somatic hypermutation grafting. Germline IGHV3-53 antibody HB148 (0 SHMs) neutralizes SARS-CoV-2 wild-type/Alpha/Delta (NT50 1–2 μg/mL) but escapes at Omicron BA.1. 3.04-Å crystal structure of HB148/wild-type RBD shows class-1 epitope, heavy chain 69% BSA, contacts Y421/Y453/A475; Omicron K417N/S477N/Q493R/Y505H remodels epitope. Enrichment analysis in CoV-AbDab IGHV3-53 sequences with BA.1 neutralization data identifies four consensus SHMs (VH G26E and T28I in CDR H1; VH S53P and Y58F in CDR H2). HB148-M4 (all four): ~100× KD improvement to both WT and BA.1 RBD; individual G26E/S53P/Y58F each 8–10× — approximately additive, distinct paratope-epitope contacts. Neutralizes WT/BA.1/BA.4-5 pseudoviruses (NT50 0.19–1.56 μg/mL); still no XBB.1.5 rescue at 100 μg/mL. Grafted onto four other IGHV3-53 antibodies (C1A-F10, P5A-3C8, BG4-25, LY-CoV488), M4 restores BA.1 binding for 3 of 4 (C1A-F10 exception gains WT affinity only). Structural mechanism: G26E extends contact to RBD residues 477–478, restoring interactions lost to S477N; S53P + Y58F improve interface packing. Ceiling of any single such patch is limited but a much more focused strategy than DMS for breadth-engineering. Limitations: surrogate/pseudovirus assays throughout; consensus-mining is retrospective not de novo prediction.

item.title: Inverse-design proteome mapping for Zα interactors via RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN (Poptsova lab, HSE Moscow) — YTHDC1 poly-E docks to ADAR1 Zα as a Z-RNA mimic; ProtBLIP2-SST — SaProt + Q-Former + Galactica multimodal (sequence, structure, text) protein-caption generator (Luo lab, HKUST)
item.description: Monday briefing. Two items — day is thin on antibody-specific work. First, Gromak, Shaytan, Herbert, and Poptsova (HSE University Moscow + InsideOutBio, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.08.737312, posted 2026-07-12): "inverse computational design" pipeline that repurposes the de novo binder-design stack (RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN) as a proteome-search tool. 1,200 backbones across four batches (unconditional; hotspot-conditioned on K169/K170/N173/R174/Y177; C2'-atom-of-Z-RNA custom potential; hotspot+potential hybrid); 8 sequences per backbone via ProteinMPNN (~10,000 designs); ColabFold filter pLDDT>80, iPAE<10 Å, interface backbone RMSD<3 Å — 2 Å is too strict (5 hits), 3 Å relaxation gives 11 template binders; 11 templates queried against SWISS-PROT by BLASTp (e<1e-5) yielding ~1,200 regions across 298 proteins; four-metric co-folding filter (pDockQ, pDockQ2, ipTM, ipSAE) narrows to 79 candidates; full-length AlphaFold3 modeling with ADAR1p150. Key methodological finding — global scores (ipTM, ipSAE) fail on IDR-heavy complexes; interface-local pDockQ + ≥10 Cα-Cα contact pairs (<8 Å) required for discrimination. Top hit: YTHDC1 poly-E disordered region (residues 199–254) docks into Zα basic pocket via charge complementarity mimicking Z-RNA phosphate backbone (contacts K169, K170, R174). Confirmed by 1 μs Amber ff19SB MD: binary complex equilibrates by 200 ns, global RMSD ~8 Å, Zα–poly-E interface stays <3 Å throughout; ternary +dsRNA simulation shows all four interfaces <2.5 Å across dimeric assembly; deaminase does not adopt editing-competent geometry — catalytically dormant. No wet-lab validation yet (proposed: co-IP, SPR, K169A/K170A/R174A mutagenesis). Transferable pipeline for antibody paratope-mimic discovery. Second, Zhuoyang Chen and Qiong Luo (HKUST-Guangzhou / HKUST, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.10.737551, posted 2026-07-12): ProtBLIP2-SST — BLIP-2 framework rewired for proteins bridging sequence + structure + text for free-text function captioning. Frozen SaProt encoder (structure-aware vocabulary fusing residue tokens with Foldseek 3Di structural tokens) + Q-Former with 8 learnable query tokens (initialized from BiomedBERT) + frozen Galactica-1.3B decoder with LoRA. Two-stage training: stage-1 protein-text contrastive + matching + captioning objectives (different attention masks per objective); stage-2 LoRA fine-tune Galactica for captioning. Trained on 441k Swiss-Prot protein-text pairs with paired AlphaFold-DB structures. ProtBLIP2-SST-650M average 90.83 vs ProtT3-650M 89.92 vs BLIP2+ProstT5-1.5B 90.03 on 8 retrieval metrics. Field-stratified analysis: structural information helps FUNCTION descriptions most, marginal on SUBCELLULAR LOCATION and SIMILARITY (homology is sequence-level). Ablations 35M-only. Transferable BLIP-2 recipe for connecting frozen antibody LMs (AbLang, IgLM, p-IgGen) to frozen scientific LLMs without retraining either half; captioning objective is what earns alignment.
item.itunes:summary: Gromak/Shaytan/Herbert/Poptsova (HSE Moscow + InsideOutBio, bioRxiv): inverse computational design repurposing RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN as proteome-search tool for Zα interactors. 1200 backbones × 8 ProteinMPNN sequences → ~10k designs; ColabFold filters (pLDDT>80, iPAE<10 Å, interface RMSD<3 Å) yield 11 templates; BLASTp against SWISS-PROT (e<1e-5) → ~1200 regions across 298 proteins → 4-metric filter → 79 → AlphaFold3 full-length. IDR-heavy complexes need interface-local pDockQ + ≥10 Cα-Cα contact pairs, not global ipTM/ipSAE. Top hit YTHDC1 poly-E (residues 199–254) docks Zα basic pocket via charge complementarity as Z-RNA mimic; confirmed by 1 μs Amber ff19SB MD (interface RMSD <3 Å binary, <2.5 Å ternary+dsRNA); no wet-lab validation yet. item.title: Night: ESM3 modality geometric atlas (Steenwyk, UC Berkeley, bioRxiv) — the four physical modalities fuse into a shared subspace between layers 25–35, sequence joins last after layer 28, functional-annotation stays orthogonal at every layer, universal layer-35 fusion depth across 12 organisms and 3 superkingdoms
item.description: Sunday-night single-item spotlight. Steenwyk (UC Berkeley MCB, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.08.737319, posted 2026-07-12): a geometric atlas of ESM3 (esm3-sm-open-v1, 1.4B parameters, 48 transformer layers, model dim 1536) built by running the network once per modality in isolation across five input channels (sequence, structure tokens, SS8, SASA, InterPro functional annotation) plus an all-modalities reference, and reading out the residual stream at each of 48 layers. Silhouette, linear CKA, effective rank, and linear probes on 892 human proteins with replication across 5,555 proteins from 12 organisms and 177 experimentally-solved structures. Key findings: (i) the four physical modalities begin in distinct subspaces, peak separation (silhouette 0.42) at layer 24, fuse into a shared low-dim subspace by layer 35 (silhouette 0.156); (ii) fusion is ordered — structure/SS8/SASA aligned from layer 0, sequence joins last after layer 28; (iii) functional-annotation channel never fuses (pairwise CKA 0.01–0.07 vs 0.99 for physical-vs-all), and orthogonality is content-driven not granularity- or redundancy-driven (per-residue InterPro also stays orthogonal; alignment does not track whether structure recovers enzyme class); (iv) fusion is a learned property — random-weight control shows no fusion; (v) universal across the tree of life — every one of 12 organisms peaks at layer 35 exactly (std dev 0); (vi) causal leave-one-modality-out ablation: withholding function displaces the representation ~6× less than withholding structure/sequence/SASA. Direct guide to which ESM3 layer to draw embeddings from for downstream antibody-LM work and points at a clean antibody-specific follow-up experiment. Author advisory disclosure: consultant to Anthropic PBC.
item.itunes:summary: Steenwyk (UC Berkeley MCB, bioRxiv): ESM3 (esm3-sm-open-v1, 1.4B params, 48 layers) modality-in-isolation atlas across 892 human proteins (replicated on 5,555 proteins/12 organisms and 177 experimental structures). Four physical modalities (sequence, structure, SS8, SASA) begin separate, peak silhouette 0.42 at layer 24, fuse to 0.156 at layer 35; fusion is ordered with sequence joining last after layer 28. Functional-annotation channel stays orthogonal at every layer (CKA 0.01–0.07 vs 0.99 for physical fusion) regardless of granularity or redundancy with structure. Fusion is learned (random-weight control shows none) and universal — all 12 organisms peak at layer 35 exactly. Withholding function in a causal ablation displaces the representation ~6× less than withholding structure/sequence/SASA. Direct guidance for which ESM3 layer to extract embeddings from for antibody-LM fine-tuning; antibody-specific replication is a natural follow-up.

item.title: Persistent single-state bias in AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, and BioEmu benchmarked on four multi-state proteins (Gumbart lab, Georgia Tech); Nammu — a 167M-parameter Mamba state-space protein/metagenomic foundation model beats same-corpus transformer gLM2
item.description: Two items, Sunday morning. First, Ye, Wang, Brogi, Parks, Kuo, and Gumbart (Georgia Tech, bioRxiv): benchmark of AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, and BioEmu on four canonical multi-state proteins — Pf-MATE (MATE transporter, inward/outward-open), LAO (leucine-arginine-ornithine binding protein, open/closed), SecA (ATPase translocation motor), and beta-2 adrenergic receptor (class A GPCR, active/inactive); all four predictors default to the dominant PDB state; small-molecule ligands have weak and inconsistent effects on which state is emitted, but large protein partners drive clear conformational switching; MSA-based approaches (AF-Cluster and random subsampling) recapitulate similar biases, indicating the state bias is not architecture-specific and survives across diffusion/flow-based models and MSA-manipulation strategies; state bias also present in BioEmu despite explicit ensemble training. Second, Azbijari, Wynne, David, and Thurber (Oregon State, bioRxiv): Nammu, a 167M-parameter mixed-modality Mamba state-space foundation model trained on the OpenMetaGenomic (OMG) corpus with a curriculum strategy (64M protein-only sequences, then 32M mixed-modality metagenomic contigs) at 20K context length; compared against gLM2 (mixed-modality transformer on same corpus with 37 percent more tokens); Nammu outperforms gLM2 at every taxonomic level on CAMI marine dataset and on KEGG Orthology function prediction in deep-sea MAGs; linear-scaling state-space alternative to quadratic-attention transformers for long protein/nucleotide context — architectural implications for repertoire-scale antibody language modeling.

item.title: AstraZeneca ESM-2/AlphaFold GNN for antibody self-association developability; USP-ddG unified delta-delta-G with H1N1 CR6261 case study; A-Alpha Bio Atlas 450M affinity database launch
item.description: Three items today. First, AstraZeneca in mAbs: an ESM-2 fine-tuned protein language model fused with AlphaFold residue graphs via disentangled multi-stream attention predicts CSI-BLI self-association class across 1,499 IgGs and 841 VHHs with edit-distance-controlled splits; structure-aware model achieves F1 = 0.76 for VHH and 0.57 for IgG; Shapley analysis highlights CDR charge/dipole and hydrophobicity as dominant drivers. Second, USP-ddG (Central South University, ISMB 2026 Bioinformatics): a unified delta-delta-G predictor combining ProteinMPNN inverse folding log-odds, FoldX empirical energy, and a GNN with Mixture-of-Experts plus CATH-guided Folding Ordering curriculum; best on SKEMPI v2.0 hold-out CATH test (Pearson R 0.655, AUROC 0.794); CR6261 anti-H1N1 AbBiBench case study (1,887 combinatorial mutants, 14 heavy-chain positions): Pearson R 0.658, Spearman R 0.627, +13% over BA-DDG. Third, A-Alpha Bio Atlas launch: 450 million quantitative AlphaSeq affinity measurements and 7,000+ antibody-antigen pseudo-structures as licensed Data Blocks; AlphaBind sequence-only affinity predictor; VHH Atlas Consortium now enrolling.
item.itunes:summary: AstraZeneca mAbs: ESM-2 + AlphaFold GNN predicts CSI-BLI self-association across 1,499 IgGs and 841 VHHs; VHH F1 = 0.76, IgG F1 = 0.57, edit-distance-controlled splits; Shapley: CDR charge/dipole and hydrophobicity dominant. USP-ddG (Central South University, ISMB/Bioinformatics): ProteinMPNN + FoldX + GNN with Mixture-of-Experts + CATH-guided curriculum; best on SKEMPI hold-out CATH (Pearson R 0.655, AUROC 0.794); CR6261 H1N1 AbBiBench (1,887 mutants): Pearson R 0.658, Spearman R 0.627, +13% over BA-DDG; code open. A-Alpha Bio Atlas: 450M quantitative AlphaSeq affinity measurements + 7,000+ antibody-antigen pseudo-structures as licensed Data Blocks; AlphaBind sequence-only predictor; VHH Atlas Consortium enrolling.

item.title: Evening: convergent HCDR-2 improbable mutations drive V3-glycan bnAb maturation across primates, and tandem scFv-Fc bispecific IL-7 receptor agonist engineering
item.description: Evening addition to today's episodes. First, a Science Translational Medicine paper from the Williams/Haynes groups at Duke (with Korber at Los Alamos and Shaw at Penn): 18 SHIV BG505-infected rhesus macaques recapitulate convergent HIV envelope evolution, and three develop V3-glycan broadly neutralizing antibodies. From the highest-breadth macaque, 203 members of a clonal lineage (DH1030) are isolated; DH1030 shares striking genetic, functional, and structural similarity with the human V3-glycan bnAb DH270 — most notably a glycine-to-arginine improbable mutation at HCDR2 position 56 (macaque) or 57 (human) that makes direct contact with the GDIR V3 motif and is required for heterologous neutralization in both lineages. PheBAR-seq single-cell BCR and transcriptome profiling of lymph node and spleen shows this improbable mutation is the trigger for GC exit into memory; a compensatory S114P HCDR3 mutation follows. V1-glycan-deleted Env variants prime both lineages, directly informing ongoing clinical trials of BG505-based immunogens. Second, from the Yea group at DGIST in Korea (PEDS, abstract-only): TB4, a tetravalent tandem scFv-Fc bispecific antibody, cis-engages IL-7 receptor alpha and the common gamma chain, outperforming the knobs-into-holes format in affinity and avidity, reduces receptor internalization, sustains STAT5 phosphorylation, and selectively expands CD4+ effector memory T cells with a distinct antiviral transcriptomic signature.
item.itunes:summary: Williams/Haynes/Korber/Shaw (Science Translational Medicine): 18 SHIV BG505-infected rhesus macaques recapitulate convergent HIV Env evolution; three develop V3-glycan bnAbs; DH1030 (203-member macaque lineage) shares an improbable HCDR2 Gly-to-Arg mutation at the same structural position as human DH270 — both mutations contact the GDIR V3 motif and are required for heterologous neutralization breadth. PheBAR-seq shows the improbable mutation drives GC exit to memory; V1-glycan-deleted Envs prime both human and macaque lineages. Yea/DGIST (PEDS): TB4 tetravalent tandem scFv-Fc bispecific cis-engages IL-7Ra and gc, outperforms knobs-into-holes format, reduces receptor internalization, sustains STAT5, selectively expands CD4+ effector memory T cells with antiviral transcriptomic signature.

item.title: Afternoon: a Nussenzweig-lab biophysical model for what IgD does — hinge entropy sets B-cell selection thresholds — and a 22-model zero-shot benchmark of protein language models on a real thermostability landscape from Jewett, Marks, and Notin
item.description: Afternoon add-on to today's morning episode. First, a Nussenzweig-lab preprint (with theory from Chakraborty at MIT and single-molecule from Blanchard) offers a physical answer to the sixty-year-old question of what IgD is for: single-molecule measurements show the antigen-binding arms of IgD are substantially more dynamic than IgM's, imposing an entropic cost on bivalent antigen capture. Mouse genetics — IgM-only, IgD-only, IgM+IgD, and hinge-truncated-IgD lines — confirm that the entropic penalty attenuates negative selection by self-antigen and raises the affinity threshold for positive selection into the germinal center. The B-cell-receptor hinge dynamics themselves are a tunable parameter of the selection landscape, with direct implications for repertoire modeling and affinity maturation. Second, a Jewett/Marks/Notin/Beckham preprint benchmarks 22 zero-shot protein fitness models on a real thermostability landscape: cell-free expression coupled to a gas-phase CO2 colorimetric assay produces a saturation scan of a thermostable carbonic anhydrase — 4,365 single-AA mutations across 39,285 reactions at 70C and 90C — then closes the loop by filtering a 100,000-variant ProteinMPNN library with zero-shot PLMs plus supervised heads down to 419 characterized variants, producing a best-in-class enzyme still active after 95C incubation. Directly translatable methodology for antibody developability.
item.itunes:summary: Nussenzweig-lab preprint: single-molecule dynamics show IgD antigen-binding arms are more mobile than IgM's, imposing an entropic penalty on bivalent antigen capture; mouse genetics with tailored isotype configurations (IgM-only, IgD-only, hinge-truncated IgD) show the penalty attenuates negative selection by self-antigen and raises the affinity threshold for germinal-center entry — BCR hinge dynamics are a tunable selection parameter. Jewett/Marks/Notin/Beckham: cell-free expression plus gas-phase CO2 assay maps a full single-AA saturation landscape of a thermostable carbonic anhydrase (4,365 mutations, 39,285 reactions, 70C and 90C), benchmarks 22 zero-shot protein fitness models on it, then filters a 100,000-variant ProteinMPNN library down to 419 characterized variants; best variant active after 95C incubation.

item.title: AbICL in-context learning for antibody affinity ranking, and IgG agalactosylation is anti-inflammatory not pro-inflammatory
item.description: Two items today. AbICL (arXiv) introduces in-context learning for antigen-specific antibody affinity ranking: a structural encoder paired with a context ranking head, trained with episodic meta-learning so the model can use a small support set of labeled comparisons from the same campaign at inference time without gradient updates. Outperforms ranking baselines on AbRank, with the largest gains under distribution shift and fine-grained discrimination. Second, a bioRxiv preprint from the Vermeren lab at Edinburgh challenges the dogma that agalactosylated IgG is pro-inflammatory: engineered agalactosylated immune complexes generate less neutrophil reactive oxygen species than galactosylated complexes, due to weaker Fc-gamma-receptor binding and lower AKT/p38 MAPK activation. The result suggests agalactosylation may be a compensatory anti-inflammatory mechanism rather than a driver of pathology, with direct implications for glycan engineering.
item.itunes:summary: AbICL: in-context learning for antibody affinity ranking using episodic meta-training; a structural encoder and context ranking head that uses support-set labeled comparisons at test time without fine-tuning; best gains on AbRank under distribution shift and fine-grained ranking. IgG N-glycan agalactosylation: Vermeren lab shows agalactosylated IgG immune complexes reduce neutrophil ROS production vs. galactosylated — weaker FcgammaR binding, lower AKT/p38 activation — suggesting the disease-associated glycoform is anti-inflammatory rather than pro-inflammatory.

item.title: Evening: FCRL5 as a fucose-sensitive IgG Fc receptor with an E293R selective-knockout mutation, ThermoFusion's OOD case for structure-plus-sequence delta-delta-G, and Woolfson-lab de novo bifunctional PROTACs
item.description: Fourth pass through the July seventh bio-archive drop. First, the Rispens group at Sanquin nails down the FCRL5-IgG interaction: 60-80 microMolar affinity driven by the two N-terminal FCRL5 domains with essential Fc-tail residues distinct from classical Fc-gamma receptors, considerable preference for afucosylated IgG, and — the engineering payload — E293R as a single-residue Fc mutation that selectively abrogates FCRL5 binding while preserving every classical Fc-gamma receptor. A clean companion to the morning's CD16a story. Second, ThermoFusion (Novartis, Basel) fuses ThermoMPNN 3D-structure embeddings with ESM-2 sequence embeddings for delta-delta-G prediction, holds up on out-of-distribution enzyme sequences where ThermoMPNN alone and state-of-the-art tools collapse, and stands in direct tension with the bonus round's sequence-only ESM-2 delta-Tm claim. Third, the Woolfson lab at Bristol builds a full de-novo protein-based PROTAC: a 67-residue helix-loop-helix scaffold (sc-apCC-2), a 3 nanoMolar BCL-xL binder from hot-spot grafting plus ProteinMPNN with a shape-complementarity negative-selection step yielding >1000x selectivity against MCL-1, a KLHL20 SLiM in the loop, and endogenous BCL-xL degradation in A549 cells on par with the clinical PROTAC DT2216. FCRL5 read from abstract-plus-body; ThermoFusion abstract-only (body not yet rendered); TPD paper read in full.
item.itunes:summary: Evening add-on. FCRL5 (Rispens/Sanquin): 60-80 microMolar IgG affinity via two N-terminal FCRL5 domains, distinct Fc-tail residues from classical FcgammaRs, preference for afucosylated IgG, and E293R as a single-residue Fc mutation that selectively knocks out FCRL5 binding while preserving classical Fc-gamma receptors — companion to today's morning CD16a story. ThermoFusion (Novartis) fuses ThermoMPNN structure embeddings with ESM-2 for delta-delta-G, holds up out-of-distribution where prior tools collapse, and pushes back on the bonus round's sequence-only claim. Woolfson-lab de-novo protein-based PROTAC: sc-apCC-2 helix-loop-helix scaffold, 3 nanoMolar BCL-xL binder with >1000x MCL-1 selectivity via shape-complementarity-based AlphaFold2 negative selection, KLHL20 SLiM in the loop, endogenous BCL-xL degradation in A549 on par with DT2216.

item.title: Late add: PGLD from Reddy and Krause at ETH — policy-gradient library design bridging generative sequence models and high-throughput screens, demonstrated on a broadly neutralizing influenza antibody
item.description: A short late-afternoon add-on. A bio-archive preprint posted this morning from Scott Sussex, Sai Reddy, and Andreas Krause at E-T-H Zurich introduces PGLD — Policy Gradients for Library Design — which parametrizes stochastic DNA libraries in a synthesis-aware way and optimizes the library's distribution against a specified objective. The framing bridges two poles that have dominated in-silico antibody design: deterministic per-sequence synthesis (controlled but capped by cost) and blind degenerate libraries (cheap but wasteful). PGLD closes the loop for lab-in-the-loop multi-round experiments and lets generative models be sampled at wet-lab scale. The headline demonstration: a library of roughly ten to the sixth unique sequences, synthesized for about seven hundred U-S dollars, to explore the mutation space of a broadly neutralizing influenza antibody. Take is drawn from the abstract only — the body has not yet rendered — and open questions on objective, screening readout, and paired-chain handling are noted in the segment.
item.itunes:summary: PGLD (Sussex, Reddy, Krause, E-T-H Zurich) parametrizes stochastic DNA libraries in a synthesis-aware way and optimizes them against an objective function using policy gradients, bridging generative sequence models and high-throughput screens. Enables closed-loop multi-round design and large-scale in-vitro sampling from generative models. Demonstrated on a ~10^6-sequence library synthesized at ~$700 to explore the mutation space of a broadly neutralizing influenza antibody. Segment drawn from the abstract only — body not yet rendered.

item.title: Bonus round: an AlphaFold benchmark on antibody and TCR complexes, sequence-only ESM2 for melting-temperature prediction, and a synthetic-sdAb linkage-specific ubiquitin binder
item.description: Bonus segment for July seventh. Three more items from the July sixth biorxiv drop. A Pierce-lab benchmark from U-Maryland IBBR of AlphaFold2, AlphaFold3, and increased sampling protocols across antibody-protein, antibody-peptide, and TCR-pMHC complex modeling: AF3 and sampling both help, antibody-peptide is the hardest interface class despite small antigen size, and per-case complementarity lets a model-pooling strategy lift antibody-peptide near-native success from 41% to 59%. A Genedata sequence-only paper argues that a carefully tuned ESM2-650M model beats structure-informed baselines for delta-Tm prediction — the interesting content is the ablation of loss, pooling, auxiliary supervision, and fine-tuning regime — and it stands in productive tension with the ESM+MM/GBSA benchmark from this morning's episode. And a Damgaard-lab paper reports 2A6, a synthetic-human single-domain antibody with nanomolar affinity and strict specificity for M1-linked polyubiquitin chains — the first sdAb targeting a homotypic linkage — with the AlphaFold3-predicted binding mode corroborated by saturation mutagenesis and validated across ELISA, IB, IP, and IF.
item.itunes:summary: Bonus segment for July seventh. Pierce-lab benchmark: AF3 + sampling help, antibody-peptide is the hardest class, and pooling lifts near-native success from 41% to 59%. Genedata argues a well-tuned ESM2-650M beats structure-informed methods for delta-Tm — in productive tension with today's morning ESM+MM/GBSA episode. Damgaard-lab 2A6 is the first synthetic-human sdAb with strict specificity for M1-linked polyubiquitin, with AlphaFold3 binding-mode prediction corroborated by saturation mutagenesis and validated across ELISA/IB/IP/IF.

item.title: An allosteric CD16a checkpoint that reframes ADCC engineering, CatESO differentiable enzyme design, PLM plus MM/GBSA stability triage, and a zero-shot benchmark that fails on epistasis
item.description: Four items today. A Murin/Ward-group cryo-EM and MINFLUX paper on the natural-killer-cell Fc receptor CD16a identifies the membrane-distal D1 domain as an allosteric checkpoint that gates ADCC upstream of CD3zeta phosphorylation, with a nanobody probe (C28) that rigidifies the closed state — and structure-guided D1 disruption in NK-92 cells enhances ADCC potency and killing kinetics, reframing ADCC engineering as a receptor-side lever. CatESO from the Zhang lab pulls a Kcat predictor into a differentiable end-to-end sequence-design loop under ESM-2 and ESMFold regularization, hits a median 1.52x model-predicted Kcat fold change across seven OOD enzymes at pLDDT>70, and outperforms an RFdiffusion3-LigandMPNN pipeline and ZymCtrl on activity/confidence balance. A Schrödinger benchmark in PEDS (Rhodes et al.) shows ESM log-odds (0.597 AUC) and MM/GBSA (0.685) are complementary on 174,945 mutations across 180 proteins — combined re-ranking reaches 0.743, a serious pre-filter for antibody stability triage. And a version-two update from the Kalinina group evaluates 95 zero-shot models on ProteinGym and documents that they succeed on single mutations and non-epistatic combinations but systematically fail on strongly epistatic combinations — a warning label for ranking multi-mutation antibody variants.
item.itunes:summary: CD16a D1 as an allosteric ADCC checkpoint from the Murin/Ward group (cryo-EM + MINFLUX + NK-92 engineering); CatESO differentiable enzyme sequence design via a Kcat predictor with ESM-2/ESMFold regularization; a Schrödinger PEDS benchmark showing ESM plus MM/GBSA is complementary for stability-enhancing mutation triage (0.743 AUC combined vs 0.685 MM/GBSA vs 0.597 ESM alone); and a 95-model ProteinGym benchmark documenting that zero-shot methods cannot predict the impact of strong epistasis.

item.title: Four-year drift in the human antibody repertoire, frustration-guided MSA subsampling for alternative conformations, TCR-HLA restriction from sequence, and a PLM-plus-graph fusion for cell-penetrating peptides
item.description: Four items today. A Briney/Burton follow-up in Scientific Reports resamples two donors from their landmark 10^15-10^18 accessible-repertoire study four years later: gross features (V/J usage, CDRH3 length) are conserved but fine features (V-J-D combinations, N/P junctional sequences) drift substantially — a challenge to the stationarity assumption embedded in repertoire-trained language models. SF-Cluster subsamples multiple sequence alignments by patterns of predicted local energetic frustration instead of sequence similarity, and improves alternative-conformation recovery by +15.5 pts on allosteric systems over AF-Cluster, with the effective MSA depth doing most of the work. TRIOPS predicts a TCR's restricting HLA allele from sequence alone using cross-reactivity-aware negative sampling by HLA pseudosequence similarity, hits 0.97 AUC on paired-chain TCRs, and recapitulates allele-specific HLA-A/B loss from bulk TCGA RNA-seq. DeepCPP is a template PLM-plus-residue-graph fusion for cell-penetrating peptide prediction — noteworthy less for the biology than for the architecture that is now default in this space.
item.itunes:summary: Longitudinal antibody-repertoire drift from Briney and Burton (Scripps): gross features conserved, fine features change over four years; SF-Cluster uses frustration patterns to subsample MSAs and beat AF-Cluster on alternative conformations; TRIOPS predicts TCR-HLA restriction from sequence with cross-reactivity-aware negative sampling and reads out HLA loss from bulk TCGA data; DeepCPP pairs ESM-2 with a multi-view residue graph for cell-penetrating peptides.

item.title: Immune-receptor geometry, uncertainty-aware TCR specificity, a brain-shuttle antibody mechanism, and ESM3-distilled implicit solvent
item.description: Four items today: TCR-FramePose introduces a local-frame descriptor set that decomposes TCR-pMHC docking into CDR3-local pose, with germline framework — not CDR3 sequence — organizing shared receptor placement. PRISM is an uncertainty-aware metric-learning framework for T-cell receptor specificity that abstains on out-of-distribution receptors and augments training with structure-guided synthetic sequences preserving interface energetics. A cryo-EM structure of the model brain-shuttle antibody 8D3 bound to mouse transferrin receptor 1 explains pH-dependent binding modes and small-scale avidity, guiding a graded panel of shuttle variants with different in-vivo brain penetration. Finally, an MIT group distills ESM3 into a GNN implicit solvent that drives stable MD and reproduces folding free-energy landscapes and IDP ensembles.
item.itunes:summary: TCR-FramePose local-frame descriptor for TCR-pMHC docking and CDR3 pose; PRISM uncertainty-aware TCR specificity with structure-guided synthetic augmentation; cryo-EM mechanism of the 8D3 blood-brain-barrier shuttle antibody with pH-graded variants; and knowledge distillation of ESM3 into a GNN implicit solvent for molecular dynamics.
